segments.say: Lesson 17. Design a Chat App (WhatsApp). WebSocket gateways, message routing, delivery receipts, offline push, ordering and storage at scale.

Design a messaging app like WhatsApp: real-time delivery, online/offline users, sent/delivered/read ticks, group chats, and never losing a message. Here is an analogy. A postal system where couriers hold an open line to every recipient who's home, and leave a note in the mailbox (push notification) for anyone who's out.

Why does this matter? One of the most-asked designs; tests real-time connections, storage and ordering. A few key words. WebSocket: Persistent two-way connection. Session registry: Which server each user is connected to. Fan-out: Delivering one message to many recipients. Push notification: O S-level alert when the app is closed.

segments.sec: Watch: Sending a message from A to B
segments.say: Sending a message from A to B. Each online client keeps a persistent WebSocket to a gateway server (millions of connections spread over many gateways).

segments.sec: Watch: Sending a message from A to B
segments.say: The gateway forwards to the chat service: authenticate, assign a message I D (time-sortable, for example Snowflake), dedupe by client message I D.

segments.sec: Watch: Sending a message from A to B
segments.say: Persist first (Cassandra/HBase partitioned by conversation id, sorted by message id), then ack Alice with one tick: "sent".

segments.sec: Watch: Sending a message from A to B
segments.say: Look up where Bob is connected in the session registry: Bob leads to gateway 2.

segments.sec: Watch: Sending a message from A to B
segments.say: Route to gateway 2 leads to Bob. Bob's app acks leads to "delivered" (two ticks) flows back to Alice. "Read" works the same way.

segments.sec: Watch: Sending a message from A to B
segments.say: Bob offline? Store it and send a push notification. When Bob reconnects, he syncs everything after his last seen message id.

Requirements & numbers. 1:1 and group chat, online presence, delivery and read receipts, offline delivery, media, multi-device. Say 500M D A U times 40 msgs about 20B msgs/day about 230k msgs/s; ~100 B each about 2 T B/day of text. Low latency (<200 ms), messages never lost, ordered within a conversation.

Deep dives. Connections: WebSocket gateways are stateful, so you need a registry (user leads to gateway) and graceful reconnect with resume from the last message id. Ordering: per-conversation sequence numbers or time-sortable I Ds. Clients sort and dedupe. Group chat: small groups fan out on write to each member; very large groups or channels use pull or fan-out via queues. Media: upload to object storage via pre-signed U R L and send only the reference in the message. C D N for downloads. E2E encryption (Signal protocol): the server routes ciphertext it can't read. Presence: heartbeats with T T L in Redis; publish changes only to interested contacts.

Say it in the interview. "Clients hold WebSockets to a fleet of gateways, with a Redis registry mapping user to gateway. The chat service assigns time-sortable I Ds, persists to Cassandra partitioned by conversation, acks the sender, then routes to the recipient's gateway or falls back to push notifications. Receipts are just small messages back. Reconnecting clients sync from their last message I D, media goes via object storage and C D N, and group fan-out depends on group size.".

Let's compare. Transport: WebSocket, bidirectional, low latency, server push. Message store: Cassandra / HBase, huge write volume, partition by conversation, range by time. Session registry: Redis, fast user leads to gateway lookup with T T L. I Ds: Snowflake / per-conv sequence, ordering plus uniqueness. Offline: Push (A P Ns/F C M) plus sync on reconnect, reliable delivery. Media: S3 plus C D N, offload bytes from chat path.

A likely interview question: How do you guarantee no lost messages in chat? A strong answer: Persist before acking the sender, client-generated message I Ds for idempotent retries, per-conversation ordering, delivery acks from the recipient, push for offline users, and sync from the last-seen I D on reconnect.
That's it for Design a Chat App (WhatsApp). Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
